title: Red Bloom above Cerro Tololo
caption: The Milky Way and the Gum Nebula above Cerro Tololo, Chile

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way, speckled with stars of many colors, sweeps down toward a city-lit horizon above the telescopes of Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile. It passes just by the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope on the left and the SMARTS 1.5-meter Telescope on the right, and the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds appear to the left of the Blanco dome.
Between the two telescopes a deep red glow spreads among the Milky Way's tendrils. It is the Gum Nebula, an emission nebula that shines because its gas has been ionized by the stars within it.

From our point of view the nebula contains a wealth of objects, including globular clusters, the Vela Pulsar and a supernova remnant about 11,000 years old. Emission nebulae like this often glow red because hydrogen gas gives off light at that color.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at Cerro Tololo, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the faint red nebula and star colors stand out far more than they would in person.

explore: Cerro Tololo is a Program of NSF NOIRLab. This photograph, by Tomáš Slovinský, was taken during the NOIRLab 2022 Photo Expedition, which visited all of NOIRLab's sites.
alt: The Milky Way descends toward a lit horizon between two observatory domes, with a red glow between them and the Magellanic Clouds to the left.
